source_capability: Distinguish propositions from questions, commands, open formulas, and the illustrated paradoxes; assign a truth value when meaningful.
Evaluate/build truth tables for negation, conjunction, inclusive OR, XOR, implication, biconditional; remember false-premise implication.
Translate sufficient/necessary conditions, “if,” “only if,” and “iff”; avoid importing conversational biconditional meaning into a logical implication.
Form converse, inverse, and contrapositive; distinguish equivalence to the original implication.
Parse operator precedence and parentheses in compound propositions.
Classify tautology, contradiction, contingency with a valid truth-table or algebraic justification.

Distinguish logical equivalence from biconditional; prove/simplify with identity, domination, idempotence, double negation, commutative, associative, distributive, De Morgan, absorption, negation, implication and biconditional laws; give a separating assignment when inequivalent.
Translate a knight/knave assertion and derive the consistent truth assignment.

knowledge_point: Domains, witnesses, finite and empty quantification
source_capability: Evaluate predicates and quantified statements relative to a specified domain; expand finite universal/existential quantification; supply a counterexample/witness; recognize vacuous universal truth for an empty domain.
Convert restricted quantification to unrestricted form using implication for universal and conjunction for existential; explain the incorrect existential-implication translation.
Identify bound/free variables and scopes, respect quantifier precedence, and distinguish a proposition from an open expression.
Distribute universal over conjunction and existential over disjunction; know the valid one-way implications and countermodels for the failed reverse distributions.
Negate quantified statements with quantifier De Morgan laws and propositional implication/negation laws.
Interpret/evaluate nested quantifiers, equal-type order changes, and the essential distinction between universal-existential and existential-universal order.
Translate mathematical and relational English to/from expressions with two or three variables and explicit domains.

knowledge_point: Null quantification, renaming, special swaps and polarity
source_capability: Apply null-quantification rules when the variable is not free in the other expression; rename bound variables; justify special quantifier swaps; account for polarity when moving a quantifier through an implication.
Express exactly one witness using existence plus uniqueness, not existence alone.
Negate nested quantifiers until every negation precedes a predicate, preserving restrictions and scopes.
Define validity as no assignment with all premises true and conclusion false; prove a valid argument or refute with such an assignment.
Construct a formal derivation with modus ponens/tollens, hypothetical/disjunctive syllogism, addition, simplification, conjunction, resolution, and equivalence; cite valid preceding lines.
Use universal/existential instantiation and generalization, including arbitrary versus particular witnesses; combine these with propositional inference.

knowledge_point: Axiom, theorem, lemma, corollary, conjecture, proof
source_capability: Distinguish axiom, theorem, lemma, corollary, conjecture, and proof at elementary definition level.
Write a direct proof using taught definitions of odd integer, perfect square, rational number; select premises and exhibit integer witnesses correctly.
Write a proof by contraposition, negate a disjunctive conclusion correctly, and use parity or the elementary product-bound example.
Write a contradiction proof of a statement or conditional, identify incompatible conclusions, and distinguish its starting assumptions from contraposition; the square-root-of-two proof is taught.
Prove a biconditional in both directions or prove a cycle of implications establishing several statements equivalent.

knowledge_point: Set notation, membership, subsets and cardinality
source_capability: Use membership, roster/set-builder notation, standard number sets, empty/singleton sets, equality, subset/proper subset, finite cardinality; distinguish an empty set from a singleton containing it.

knowledge_point: Finite power sets and empty-set edge cases
source_capability: Enumerate power sets, including empty-set edge cases, and use finite size 2^n.
Use ordered tuples and Cartesian products; recognize a relation as an arbitrary subset of a product. No additional relation properties are taught here.

knowledge_point: Finite/indexed set operations and union size
source_capability: Compute/interpret finite and indexed unions/intersections, disjointness, difference, complement relative to a stated universe, and the two-set union-size identity.

knowledge_point: Set identities by membership and logic
source_capability: Prove or refute set identities using element membership or corresponding logic laws, including De Morgan, absorption, distribution, complement and identity laws.

knowledge_point: Functions, domain/codomain, range, image and preimage
source_capability: Identify a function's domain, codomain, image/preimage, range, and exactly-one-output condition.
Prove/refute injectivity and surjectivity using domain/codomain; recognize bijection and distinguish “one-to-one” from “one-to-one correspondence.”
Determine invertibility, construct an inverse for a bijection, and explain why non-bijections lack a function inverse on the stated codomain.
Compose compatible functions in the correct order; calculate both orders and recognize that they can differ.
Define equal infinite cardinality by bijection; classify finite, countably infinite and uncountable; construct enumerations/bijections for naturals, positive/even integers and all integers.

knowledge_point: Rationals, finite strings and finite products
source_capability: Enumerate rationals and finite-alphabet finite strings; use diagonal traversal/layers and finite products N^k, with duplicate rational representations handled.

knowledge_point: Uncountability, real diagonal and infinite sequences
source_capability: Apply/prove real-interval uncountability by diagonalization; compare cardinality using injections and absence of bijection; distinguish finite strings from infinite sequences; handle decimal-representation ambiguity.

Recognize the continuum hypothesis's statement and the slide's claim that it cannot be proved/disproved in ZFC. This is a brief concept/recognition check only, never a proof demand or an assertion that CH is established true.
State/use Schröder-Bernstein: injections both ways imply equal cardinality; construct suitable injections for simple interval sets. Its proof is not taught.
Establish |S|<|P(S)|: singleton injection plus diagonal subset excluding any proposed surjection; derive uncountability of P(N).

Define computable/uncomputable and prove existence of uncomputable N-to-{0,1} functions by countable programs versus uncountably many subsets/functions; recognize the halting problem as the named example only.
Apply sequential/product rule with valid conditional choice counts, including sampling without reuse.
Count arbitrary and injective functions between finite sets; handle impossible injection when domain is larger.
Exhibit a subset-to-bit-string bijection and derive the finite power-set count.
Count exact multiplications in the taught rectangular triple-loop matrix multiplication; no general complexity theory required.
Apply disjoint sum rule, split by length/cases, combine sum/product rules, and use complement/subtraction for forbidden choices or at least one required character.

knowledge_point: Finite branching trees and stopping rules
source_capability: Construct/count a finite branching tree for restricted bit strings or a playoff that stops at its winning threshold; do not count illegal continuations.
State/prove ordinary pigeonhole principle, identify objects/boxes, use noninjectivity, and apply to birthdays, scores, partitions, and parity matching.
Use ceiling(n/k) generalized pigeonhole bound; derive a minimum forcing a multiplicity, distinguish an unspecified box from a specified box, and solve capacity/area-code problems.
Count full and k-permutations of distinct objects, ordered selections, prize assignments, and arrangements with a fixed first item.
Count arrangements containing a specified contiguous block using block compression.
Count circular arrangements modulo rotation with fixed neighbor direction; do not identify reflections unless explicitly asked.
Count k-combinations, derive P(n,k)=C(n,k)k!, use symmetry/complements, count fixed-weight strings, and select mixed committees.
Give a combinatorial proof or explicit bijection showing that two expressions count the same objects; complement bijection proves combination symmetry.
Count permutations with indistinguishable repeated types via n!/(n1!...nk!).

Allocate distinguishable objects to distinguishable boxes with prescribed sizes; derive the multinomial formula, including a leftover box, and explain its correspondence to repeated-type permutations.

knowledge_point: Stars and bars and unordered repeated selections
source_capability: Use stars and bars for indistinguishable objects in distinguishable boxes, repetitions, nonnegative integer-sum solutions, and unlimited-type selections. Explicitly define whether zero occupancy is allowed.

knowledge_point: Binomial theorem and signed coefficient extraction
source_capability: State/justify the binomial theorem; extract signed/scaled coefficients and constant terms, solving the exponent condition.

knowledge_point: Subset sums and weighted binomial sums
source_capability: Derive subset sum 2^n, alternating sum 0, even/odd subset equality, and weighted sum 3^n by substitution or combinatorial reasoning.

knowledge_point: Pascal identity triangle and monotone paths
source_capability: Prove/apply Pascal's identity, construct Pascal's triangle with boundary values, and count monotone right/down paths via its recurrence.
Prove/apply Vandermonde by splitting a selection between two disjoint groups and summing over every feasible split.
Derive/apply sum_k C(n,k)^2=C(2n,n) as the taught Vandermonde corollary.
Prove/apply hockey-stick identity C(n+1,r+1)=sum_(j=r)^n C(j,r), using last-one position or maximum selected label.

knowledge_point: General inclusion-exclusion and its multiplicity proof
source_capability: Apply two-, three-, and n-set inclusion-exclusion; count divisible integers using intersections; justify the general formula by counting an element in r sets and the binomial alternating identity.
Count onto functions/job assignments by excluding missing target values and counting intersections of missing-target sets.
Recognize derangements; derive/use D_n=n! sum_(j=0)^n (-1)^j/j! through fixed-point intersections.
Count permutations with exactly a prescribed number of fixed points by selecting them and deranging the remainder; notice impossible remainder size one.
Convert derangement counts to probability D_n/n! and recognize its approach to 1/e. No analytic limit proof is taught.

knowledge_point: Finite sample spaces and uniform ordered/unordered sampling
source_capability: Define experiment/outcome/sample space/event; count probabilities only under equally likely finite outcomes; handle cards/lottery and ordered draws with/without replacement.

knowledge_point: Complement, inclusion-exclusion and disjoint probability sums
source_capability: Use complements, two-/n-event inclusion-exclusion, and addition for pairwise-disjoint events; justify via set identities.

knowledge_point: Nonuniform discrete probability mass functions and event masses
source_capability: Validate a discrete pmf by nonnegativity and total one; distinguish uniform/nonuniform distributions; sum outcome masses for an event.
Test independence with P(E intersection F)=P(E)P(F) and construct/check a small finite model; distinguish independence from mere disjointness.
Distinguish pairwise from mutual independence; check all required intersections and demonstrate pairwise-but-not-mutual using the taught coin/XOR-type example.

knowledge_point: Conditional probability on a restricted sample space
source_capability: Compute conditional probability as joint probability divided by positive conditioning probability, using the correct restricted sample space.

knowledge_point: Conditional chain rule and birthday collision threshold versus certainty
source_capability: Apply the sequential conditional chain rule; use complement and the no-collision product for the birthday problem; distinguish certainty from probability exceeding a threshold.

knowledge_point: Total probability over an exhaustive disjoint partition
source_capability: Compute total probability across a mutually exclusive exhaustive partition; combine known/unknown cases or multiple source populations.

knowledge_point: Independence as unchanged conditional probability with positive denominator
source_capability: Relate event independence to unchanged conditional probability, explicitly requiring the relevant conditioning event to have positive mass.

knowledge_point: Ordinary/generalized Bayes with prior and observation likelihood
source_capability: Apply ordinary/generalized Bayes with priors and likelihoods; distinguish forward and posterior probabilities; model false positives/negatives, urn selection, spam counts, and defective products.

knowledge_point: Monty Hall host likelihoods, posteriors and policy success
source_capability: Build a Monty Hall observation likelihood from an explicit host policy; compute posterior, choose stay/switch under uniform or nonuniform priors, and compute a policy's overall success probability.

knowledge_point: Random variable as a deterministic function and induced distribution
source_capability: Define a random variable as a deterministic real-valued function on outcomes; derive its distribution by summing the masses of outcomes with the same value.

knowledge_point: Bernoulli/binomial model, exact/interval probabilities and normalization
source_capability: Define Bernoulli trials and binomial distribution with independent equal-success-probability trials; calculate exact and interval probabilities, and check normalization using the binomial theorem.

knowledge_point: Density, point probability and interval area
source_capability: Distinguish a density from a probability; express an interval probability as area/integral; recognize the displayed normal density as an example. A simple constant-density interval suffices.

knowledge_point: Geometric stopping law on positive integers, normalization, tails and mean
source_capability: Model countably infinite stopping-time outcomes and geometric distribution on {1,2,...}; normalize by geometric series, calculate masses/tails, and use expectation 1/p for 0<p<=1.

knowledge_point: Expected values by outcomes/distribution and binomial mean
source_capability: Compute expected value by sample outcomes or the induced distribution; recognize binomial expectation np.

knowledge_point: Linearity, affine expectation and indicators without independence
source_capability: Prove/apply linearity and affine expectation; use indicator mean P(event); independence is not required for linearity.

knowledge_point: Hatcheck fixed-point indicators with dependent assignments
source_capability: Derive expected correct hats by dependent fixed-point indicators, yielding one; avoid demanding independence of the indicators.

knowledge_point: Hiring via record indicators under a uniform permutation
source_capability: Model hires as record indicators under uniformly random distinct candidate ranks; mean of indicator i is 1/i and total mean is the harmonic sum.

knowledge_point: Empty bins via independent ball placements and dependent bin indicators
source_capability: Compute expected empty bins with independent uniform ball placements: n(1-1/n)^m; distinct bin-emptiness indicators need not be independent.

knowledge_point: Average-case linear search and explicitly counted insertion-sort shifts
source_capability: Define average-case cost relative to an input distribution; calculate expected successful linear-search position and expected insertion-sort cost under uniformly random permutations. Cost convention must be explicit; see source defect below.
Model coupon collection as a sum of geometric stages with success probability (n-i)/n; derive n times the harmonic sum, using independent uniform coupon draws.

knowledge_point: Joint-mass independence and product expectation versus dependent counts
source_capability: Define independent random variables by every joint-value mass factorization; prove/use E(XY)=E(X)E(Y) under independence; contrast dependent heads/tails with linearity.

knowledge_point: Variance identity, standard deviation and affine variance scaling
source_capability: Compute variance/standard deviation from definitions or E(X^2)-E(X)^2; derive the identity and variance scaling; calculate Bernoulli/die variance and distinguish E(X^2) from E(X)^2.

knowledge_point: Pairwise-independent variance addition, weighted sums and binomial variance
source_capability: Derive/use Bienayme variance addition for pairwise independent variables, square coefficients for weighted sums, and obtain binomial variance np(1-p).

knowledge_point: Expectation and variance of independent repeated-measurement means
source_capability: Compute the expectation and variance of the mean of independent repeated measurements: mean mu and variance sigma^2/n; explain the role of independence and scaling.
